newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: NAVAN HALF-YEAR PRE-TAX PROFIT 0.16 MLN.
newsitem.headline: NAVAN HALF-YEAR PRE-TAX PROFIT 0.16 MLN.

text.p: Six months to June 30, 1996
(million $ unless stated)
Shr (cents) 0.31 loss vs 6.67 profit
Pretax profit 0.16 vs 5.24
Turnover 12.84 vs 13.04
Operating profit 0.07 vs 1.09
Exceptional nil vs 4.01 gain
Currency adjustment 0.52 loss vs 0.14 loss
Interest receivable 0.66 vs 0.48
Tax charge 0.34 vs 0.10
Net taxed 0.17 loss vs 5.14 profit
Retained 0.18 loss vs 2.43 profit
NOTE - Exploration group Navan Resources Plc, which
operates the Chelopech copper mine in Bulgaria, said the recent
fall in the price of copper adversely affected its half-year
results.
Navan's retained loss of $0.18 million was arrived at after
a provision of $1 million against the value of copper
concentrates in transit, a foreign exchange loss of $516,000
and a tax charge of $338,000.
The $1 million provision against concentrates reflects the
fall in metal prices from time of shipment to the final sales
value date, Navan said.
The collapse of the copper price in May has meant that the
average price realised per tonne of copper sold has dropped
from $2,923 in 1995 to $2,085 for the first six months of 1996.
The foreign exchange losses of $516,000 resulted mainly
from the massive devaluation of the Bulgarian lev over the six
months from 70 to 155 to the US dollar, Navan said.
While this devaluation combined with the Bulgarian banking
crisis and high inflation has made for difficult for business
operating conditions, Navan said it expected to see benefits in
lower operating costs at the Chelopech mine.
Navan also said its exposure to currency devaluations
continues to be limited as effectively as possible with the
Bulgarian sales, cash reserves and loans being in US dollars.
